entry_conditions: Supported earliest entry is already handle-attached, not red-attached: measured drawer position about 0.1863 m increasing at about 0.107 m/s, TCP near [-0.3263, 0, 0.1279] m and individual finger qpos about 0.0071 m. TCP-X plus drawer position is approximately -0.140 m and changes little as the drawer opens. Supported later entries include handle release and free motion with fingers near 0.040 m, red approach/closure toward about 0.0182 m per finger, and established red lift. The two causal observations contain qpos[0:9], qvel[9:18], world TCP/red/blue poses [18:25]/[25:32]/[32:39] with wxyz quaternions, drawer position/velocity [39:41] and goals [41:47]. Pose history and aperture jointly support inferred attachment identity; a negative gripper command alone is not contact evidence and previous commands are not part of this model's observation input. These measured values describe training support, not hard acceptance thresholds.
exit_conditions: An early outgoing-overlap transfer can occur during red descent over the pad, but only to a successor covering descent and release. Red containment alone is not manipulation readiness: closed fingers may still carry red slightly above the task height. After opening, red stays around z=0.020 m while the TCP subsequently rises, so red rigidity should no longer apply. The full suffix ends during continuous blue lift: measured blue center z is about 0.139-0.146 m, TCP is about 9-10 mm on blue's negative world-X side, individual fingers are about 0.0182 m and demonstrated g=-1. Red is near [-0.176, -0.298, 0.020] m and the drawer is still about 0.297 m open. A useful late transfer preserves blue attachment. No release, clearance, speed or sustained-hold condition is added to the supplied simultaneous drawer/red/blue task-success contract.
overlap_role: This model learns the entire expanded action slice, not only red transport. Incoming overlap with open_access starts at 195 and extends through red acquisition/initial lift around 474-476, changing handle coupling to free motion to red coupling. Outgoing overlap with insert_blue begins around 575-582 and extends to endpoints 845-859, changing red descent/attachment to released red and then blue attachment. All phases retain ordinary diffusion imitation and future-state supervision. The learned causal attachment posterior and continuous transform refinement condition one joint-action denoiser; uncertain training-only co-motion masks activate predicted block rigidity or handle X coupling without forcing either during open-finger retreat. No fixed route clock or policy schedule is implemented.
successor_readiness: Pass two causal physical observations in the same world-metre/wxyz interface so the insertion policy can re-estimate the TCP/object transform, finger opening and object motion. Do not substitute this model's private posterior or transform latent for physical history. Early takeover requires an insertion policy able to finish red descent, release and retreat before blue acquisition. Late takeover should continue an already-gripped blue lift without an artificial release. Confirm red-on-pad and retained drawer opening from actual observations rather than only the attachment estimate. The reported terminal blue lift is successor readiness, not final blue-inside completion.
failure_signatures: During intended transport, tool-relative object translation/rotation drifts substantially; TCP rises while the intended block remains on its support; inferred attachment changes identity without an intervening opening; red is incorrectly dragged or modeled as attached during empty retreat; drawer closes instead of retaining access. Closed fingers and co-motion remain indirect evidence, not proof of a secure grasp. Asymmetric finger qvel appears in successful red and blue grasps, including demo1010, and is not sufficient evidence of slip. These are diagnostic cues for the inference agent, not implemented recovery controllers or learned performance claims.
continuation_guidance: Choose duration from the observed transition. Continue for remaining handle pull/release, red acquisition or placement, and any demonstrated release/retreat/blue pickup phase not yet delegated to a suitable successor. Around demo1000 575 red is still descending at z about 0.211 m; around 605 it is still held near z=0.0323 m. Around 615 it has settled at z=0.0200 m and fingers are open but TCP retreat need not yet have occurred. The expanded policy supports continuing through empty retreat and blue initial lift. Transfer earlier only if the successor supports the unfinished overlap; transfer late with closed fingers and blue co-motion preserved. Fixed eight-action execution and DDPM sampling are framework-owned; the model does not implement adaptive prefix selection or hard semantic transitions.
limitations: Two-frame history may not distinguish stationary support, pushing and secure attachment. No direct contact, image, prior-command, FK or IK input is available. Labels and masks use empirical proximity/aperture/co-motion tolerances, and auxiliary action-to-state dynamics is learned rather than physically exact. No universal 9 mm grasp offset, strict rigidity guarantee, dropped-object recovery, regrasp, slip recovery or greater handoff-error tolerance is established. The full expanded training slice supports the named transitions but cannot prove learned execution success. Invoke a different supported policy rather than assuming this policy covers arbitrary off-demonstration recovery or final blue insertion beyond its slice.
